messages:
olivia: Quick note from onboarding calls today: multiple users hit the same import confusion. Quickstart shows `require('@redwood/inference')` and the sample app uses `import { Redwood } from '@redwood/inference'` — neither matches our published types.

ben: Yep. I just triaged two tickets. Error patterns: `TypeError: Redwood is not a constructor` or `ReferenceError: require is not defined` when they deploy to edge.

kai: TL;DR: package currently exposes named exports (RedwoodClient, createClient) in ESM build. No default export. CJS consumers get an object when using require. Example: `const { RedwoodClient } = require('@redwood/inference')` works, but `const Redwood = require('@redwood/inference')` doesn't do what docs imply.

olivia: New devs are copy/pasting the README sample into a Next.js app (Edge API routes) and hitting require issue. We need a one-paragraph "Edge gotcha" plus explicit Quickstart variants: Node server, Next.js serverless (CJS), Next.js Edge (ESM), Cloudflare Workers (ESM).

ben: Also a common pitfall: people put async secret retrieval at module scope like `const client = new RedwoodClient({ apiKey: await getSecret() })`. In serverless cold-starts that can be undefined. Suggestion: show lazy init inside handler and a minimal retry/countdown wrapper.

kai: Example lazy init snippet for docs: 
```js
import { RedwoodClient } from '@redwood/inference';
let client;
export default async function handler(req) {
  if (!client) {
    const apiKey = process.env.RW_API_KEY; // sync
    client = new RedwoodClient({ apiKey });
  }
  return client.generate({ prompt: 'hello' });
}
```

olivia: Good. Also add an explicit TypeScript example and note the correct type import: `import type { RedwoodClient } from '@redwood/inference'` and instantiation `const client = new RedwoodClient(...)`. Users were trying `new Redwood()` because of outdated README samples.

ben: UX trade: adding a default export `export default RedwoodClient` would make the common `import Redwood from '@redwood/inference'` work, but could mask named-export patterns and slightly affect tree-shaking. Thoughts?

kai: If we add `export default RedwoodClient`, keep the named exports too. Update types to include `export default`. That should be backwards-compatible for JS consumers and less confusing. I'll add a SDK PR proposal.

olivia: Meanwhile docs PR to ship today with these changes: 1) split quickstart into three tabs (Node CJS, Node ESM, Edge), 2) emphasise no `require` in Edge + show how to detect runtime, 3) add small troubleshooting checklist for import/type errors, 4) show safe auth patterns and a retry snippet.

docs-bot: Draft docs PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/855 "quickstart: imports + edge". Preview: https://preview.docs/quickstart/imports-edge

support-bot: Created ticket INF-1983 linking user logs and repro.

ben: One last nuance — bundlers. Add short note about package.json fields: `main` points to CJS build, `module` points to ESM; some bundlers honor `browser` field. Docs should recommend using ESM for modern stacks and CJS for older Node projects.

olivia: Cool. Kai, can you post the SDK PR number here when you open it? I'll merge the docs once PR preview looks good.

kai: Will do. Opening SDK PR now to add `export default` and update types. PR link to follow.

olivia: Thanks everyone — this should cut a steady stream of onboarding confusion. :raised_hands:
